Support the Finance Manager with the full accounting cycle, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger.
Process and record all financial transactions accurately and in a timely.
Perform monthly bank and credit card reconciliations.
Send invoices and contracts promptly to customers.
Follow up on late invoices.
Maintain the general ledger, ensuring all entries are accurate and coded correctly.

Implement and maintain internal financial controls and procedures.
Handle confidential information with the utmost discretion.

Proven experience (typically 2+ years) working as a Full Charge Bookkeeper or in a similar comprehensive accounting role.
Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
In-depth knowledge of accounting principles and procedures (GAAP).
Expert proficiency in QuickBooks Online, Bill.com, and Stripe.
Highly proficient in Microsoft Excel (VLOOKUP, Pivot Tables, etc.) and other Microsoft Office Suite applications.
Experience in creating dashboards and board presentations.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

This position is critical to ensuring accurate, compliant, timely, and well-controlled compensation for our workforce across Poland, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Norway, Spain, and Sweden, in line with each country's statutory pay cycle.

Payroll Processing & Systems Management
Own the day-to-day end-to-end payroll process for employees across Poland, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Norway, Spain, and Sweden, partnering with in-country payroll providers and ADP Celergo and operating within the agreed governance and approval framework. Manage day-to-day relationships with ADP Celergo, assigned in-country payroll providers, and Employer of Record (EOR) providers; monitor delivery against agreed service levels; resolve operational issues; and escalate material service, compliance, contractual, or commercial concerns to the Global Payroll Manager.
Maintain and monitor the international payroll calendar, including input deadlines, review dates, approval deadlines, funding dates, statutory payment dates, and year-end requirements.
Prepare each payroll for approval, including a clear summary of material changes, exceptions, funding requirements, reconciliations, and identified risks, and obtain final approval from the Global Payroll Manager and other designated approvers before payroll or payment release.
Operate in accordance with segregation-of-duties requirements so that no individual can independently prepare, approve, and release the same payroll or payment.
Review and audit timesheets, attendance records, annual leave/PTO balances, and other country-specific inputs (e.g., UK statutory sick/maternity pay, Nordic parental leave, Spanish IRPF adjustments) to ensure accurate and compliant payment calculations prior to each payroll run.
Coordinate and execute approved off-cycle payroll runs, retroactive pay adjustments, and manual payments across multiple countries and currencies, ensuring appropriate justification, review, approval, funding, and audit evidence.
Oversee country-specific statutory deductions and employer obligations, including UK PAYE/National Insurance, Polish ZUS and PIT, Norwegian tax and folketrygd contributions, Spanish Seguridad Social and IRPF, Swedish tax and arbetsgivaravgifter, and Singapore CPF, in full compliance with applicable local laws.

Support and monitor integrations and data flows between ADP Celergo, in-country payroll vendors, the general ledger, Workday HR, and benefits platforms, ensuring data integrity across multiple currencies, languages, and statutory calendars and escalating interface failures promptly.
